text:
maria: infra-bot alerted: sustained latency spike across us-west-2 runtime pool starting ~1771345000. p95 spiked to 820ms, throughput dropped ~35% :eyes:
infra-bot: [ALERT] runtime_usw2_p95_latency > 700ms for 5m (group=prod-runtime-pool-3)
maria: seeing huge KV cache eviction rate in runtime logs around same time. traces for many requests are blank (no spans) — looks like tracer sampler dropped them.
devon: copying logs, attached snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T21:52:13Z] evict: shard=12 keys=1247 -> evicted=983 reason=noisy_neighbor
[2026-03-17T21:52:15Z] kernel_select: selected=fast_matmul_v2 fallback=slow_gemm (heuristic_score=0.42)
[2026-03-17T21:52:16Z] batch: size=1 latency=150ms reason=early_flush
[2026-03-17T21:52:17Z] kvcache: lookup_miss user=tenant-101 key=ctx:abcd
```
devon: interesting bit: kernel_select chooses fast_matmul_v2 but we see batch size=1 and early flushes — fast_matmul_v2 is optimized for large batch sizes, performance regresses when batch is tiny.
lee: is this correlated with noisy neighbors on that GPU host? any MIG oversubscription logs?
sam: yes, host-gpu-45 shows concurrent 4th-party job (partner-batch) that spiked GPU utilization. I saw CUDA SM utilization jump from 15% to 95% at 21:52.
olivia: Grafana dashboard for kernel-level ops shows selector hit-rate dropping and fallback_count rising, but the traces panel is almost empty. dashboard freshness also says last scrape 2m ago :thinking: 
maria: I pushed trace sampler bump to 0.005 -> 0.05 when we thought traffic was low last week. wonder if that changed effective sampling during burst.
devon: that would explain blank traces. if sampler is low we miss the very requests that are impacted (short but expensive kernels) — observability blindspot.
lee: quick mitigation: moving noisy tenant off pool and force kernel fallback to conservative selection. I'm spinning a pod replace to cordon host-gpu-45. On it.
deploy-bot: rolling restart for node host-gpu-45 initiated by lee (reason=noisy-neighbor eviction)
sam: also temporarily lowered batch_early_flush_threshold from 20ms -> 80ms in runtime config for prod-runtime-pool-3 to avoid flushing tiny batches. patch applied to canary.
devon: ack. can we also disable fast_matmul_v2 for small batch sizes? the kernel selector heuristic should consider current batch distribution, not just static metrics.
olivia: opened INF-4123 to track long-term: "kernel selector sensitivity to skewed batch size + KV evictions causing perf regressions" https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4123
maria: checklist for postmortem: 1) why did KV cache evict so aggressively 2) how did sampler config change hide traces 3) adjust selector heuristics and add metric to signal "selector mismatch"
devon: preliminary profiling results from canary (after batch threshold change): p95 dropped from 820ms -> 190ms, throughput back to ~95% baseline. kernel selector fallback rate reduced by 60%.
sam: kvcache metrics: working set size for tenant-101 exceeded expected because partner-batch job pinned a bunch of prefixes. need eviction policy tune (prefer LRU with tenant backpressure).
lee: note: log sampling was also sampling error logs at 5% only for runtime. I bumped to 50% for error-level logs in cluster until infra issue resolved.
olivia: dashboards mismatched because prom scrape of runtime-exporter had label relabel config changed last week. I reverted that relabel temporarily to restore proper per-tenant panels.
maria: action items (short):
- infra: audit noisy workloads on us-west-2, add admission controls (sam)
- runtime: change kernel selector to include live batch distribution and KV miss rate as features (devon)
- telemetry: increase min trace sampler to 0.01 on all prod pools and create alert for trace-drop ratio (olivia)
- product: notify affected customers if we have rollback incidents (maria)
olivia: created follow-ups: INF-4123 (kernel selector), INF-4124 (kvcache eviction policy), INF-4125 (tracing-sampling-rollback)
lee: re: noisy neighbor prevention, I'm going to add GPU-level cgroup limits for non-redwood workloads in shared pools. PR incoming.
maria: final note: this incident exposed a couple observability gaps: 1) sampling configs live-changed without guardrails, 2) dashboards rely on scraped labels that can be accidentally mutated, 3) selector heuristics lack a "confidence" metric to trigger conservative fallback. Add these to the postmortem.
oncall-bot: incident-deck created: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/1771345123 - owners assigned: maria, devon, sam
devon: thanks — I'll start a small benchmark reproducer that simulates 1) skewed batch sizes + 2) KV churn + 3) kernel candidate mix. want to validate selector ML before rolling to prod.
maria: thanks everyone. i'll update the incident deck with timeline and will ping when the postmortem is ready. :thumbsup:
